whatYouMustDo: Make a list of every AI system you build or use, and note what each one does.
Work out each system's risk level: banned, high, limited, or minimal.
Check the banned list again before 2 December 2026: it now also covers AI that generates child sexual abuse material or non-consensual sexual or intimate images.

For high-risk AI, run a risk assessment, use good quality data, keep technical documentation, allow human oversight, and test for accuracy and security. You have until 2 December 2027 for stand-alone Annex III systems, and 2 August 2028 for AI inside regulated products.
Tell people clearly when they are dealing with AI. From 2 December 2026, AI-generated or manipulated content must also carry a machine-readable mark.
Train your staff so they understand the AI they work with.
If you have under 750 staff and turnover of 150 million euros or less, check the new 'small mid-cap' category: it brings simplified documentation and lighter penalties.
keyDates: Banned AI practices: enforced since 2 February 2025.
General-purpose AI model rules: since 2 August 2025.
General application, including the transparency duties (Art. 50): 2 August 2026.
New bans on AI-generated child sexual abuse material and non-consensual intimate imagery, and machine-readable marking of AI-generated content (Art. 50(2)): 2 December 2026.
Regulatory sandboxes in place in each member state: 2 August 2027.
High-risk rules for stand-alone Annex III systems: 2 December 2027 (deferred from 2 August 2026 by the Digital Omnibus).
High-risk rules for AI built into regulated products (Annex I, e.g. medical devices, machinery, toys): 2 August 2028.
Legacy AI systems used by public authorities: 2 August 2030.
eu_ai_act.penalties: Up to 35 million euros or 7% of worldwide annual turnover for banned practices; up to 15 million euros or 3% for most other breaches.

whatYouMustDo: Have a clear legal reason before you use anyone's personal data in AI.
Tell people, in plain language, how their data is used.
If the AI makes important decisions about people on its own, give them a way to get a human review.
Do a data protection impact assessment for high-risk AI processing.
Use only the data you need, keep it accurate, and do not keep it longer than necessary.
keyDates: In force across the EU since 25 May 2018.
gdpr.penalties: Up to 20 million euros or 4% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.

whatYouMustDo: Design connected products so users can easily get the data they generate.
When a user asks, share their data with a third party on fair terms.
Remove unfair data clauses from your contracts with smaller businesses.
Let customers switch to another cloud provider without heavy obstacles or fees.
keyDates: In force; the main rules apply since 12 September 2025.
eu_data_act.penalties: Set by each EU country; in Germany the Federal Network Agency can impose administrative fines.

whatYouMustDo: If you run a data-sharing service, register it and keep it neutral.
Follow the rules when you reuse protected public-sector data to train AI.
If you collect data for altruistic purposes, meet the transparency requirements.
keyDates: Applies since 24 September 2023.
dga.penalties: Set by each EU country; administrative fines and possible loss of registration for data services.

whatYouMustDo: Put a written technology and AI risk-management framework in place, owned by senior management.
Detect, classify and report major IT incidents to your regulator within the deadlines.
Test the resilience of your critical systems regularly.
Manage and document the risks from your outside IT and AI suppliers, with a clear exit plan.
keyDates: Applies since 17 January 2025.
dora.penalties: Supervisory measures and fines set by national regulators; in Germany this is BaFin.

whatYouMustDo: Put cybersecurity risk-management measures in place that match your level of risk.
Get senior management to approve the measures and take training.
Report significant incidents to the BSI: an early warning within 24 hours, a fuller report within 72 hours, and a final report within one month.
Check the security of your suppliers and service providers.
keyDates: The German implementing law has been in force since 5 December 2025.
nis2.penalties: Up to 10 million euros or 2% of worldwide turnover for essential entities.

whatYouMustDo: Build your product to be secure from the start, with no known exploitable weaknesses at release.
Provide security updates for the product's support period.
Report actively exploited weaknesses and serious incidents to the authorities on time.
Complete a conformity assessment and add the CE marking before you sell it.
keyDates: In force; reporting duties from September 2026; main duties from 11 December 2027.
cra.penalties: Up to 15 million euros or 2.5% of worldwide turnover.

whatYouMustDo: Treat software and AI as products that can be defective, and keep evidence of safety and testing.
Be ready to disclose technical information if someone claims your AI product harmed them.
Review your insurance and contracts for AI-related liability.
keyDates: In force at EU level since 9 December 2024.
Germany passed its implementing law (the new Product Liability Act) in October 2026; it applies from 9 December 2026.
pld.penalties: Civil liability: you may have to pay compensation for damage caused by a defective product.

whatYouMustDo: Run a safety risk assessment for your machine, including any self-learning AI behaviour.
Build in safety functions and keep technical documentation.
Complete the conformity assessment and CE marking before sale.
Watch for the European Commission's delegated acts that will add AI-specific requirements for machinery.
keyDates: Applies from 20 January 2027.
AI-specific requirements for machinery will be added by the European Commission through delegated acts, to apply by 2 August 2028 (Digital Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744).
machinery.penalties: National market-surveillance measures, fines, and product withdrawal.

whatYouMustDo: Explain the main factors your recommender system uses to rank content.
Offer users an option that is not based on profiling, where required.
Be transparent about content moderation and give reasons for your decisions.
Larger platforms must assess and reduce the systemic risks from their algorithms.
keyDates: Fully applicable since 17 February 2024.
dsa.penalties: Up to 6% of worldwide annual turnover for very large platforms.

whatYouMustDo: If you are a gatekeeper, do not rank your own services ahead of others unfairly.
Do not use business users' data to compete against them.
Keep ranking fair and non-discriminatory.
keyDates: Applies since 2 May 2023; gatekeeper duties from March 2024.
dma.penalties: Up to 10% of worldwide turnover, rising to 20% for repeat breaches.

whatYouMustDo: If you offer identity or trust services, meet the security and registration rules.
If you rely on electronic identity or the EU wallet for KYC or anti-fraud, use compliant providers.
Keep your identity-verification AI auditable.
keyDates: Original rules from 2014; eIDAS 2.0 in force 2024; EU wallets rolling out by 2026.
eidas.penalties: Supervisory measures, national fines, and loss of trust-service status.

whatYouMustDo: Identify which German authority supervises your AI use (often the Federal Network Agency).
Be ready for market-surveillance checks under the EU AI Act.
Consider the regulatory sandbox if you are developing new AI.
keyDates: Passed by the Bundestag on 11 June 2026 and approved by the Bundesrat on 10 July 2026.
In force since 29 July 2026 (Federal Law Gazette 2026 I No. 223).
ki_mig.penalties: Fines follow the EU AI Act's penalty levels; the KI-MIG sets how German authorities impose them.

whatYouMustDo: Follow the special German rules when you process employee data with AI.
Be careful with AI profiling of staff in hiring and performance management.
Report data breaches as required.
keyDates: In force since 25 May 2018; updated periodically.
bdsg.penalties: Follows the GDPR levels: up to 20 million euros or 4% of turnover.

whatYouMustDo: Get clear consent before placing cookies or tracking on a user's device.
Do not use AI profiling or tracking without a valid legal basis.
Keep your cookie banner and consent records compliant.
keyDates: In force since 1 December 2021; renamed TDDDG on 14 May 2024.
tdddg.penalties: Fines up to 300,000 euros for certain breaches, plus GDPR fines for related data misuse.

whatYouMustDo: Identify the AI models, datasets and prompts that are valuable secrets for your business.
Take reasonable steps to keep them secret, such as access controls and confidentiality clauses.
Use contracts when sharing confidential data with partners.
keyDates: In force since 26 April 2019.
geschgehg.penalties: Civil claims for damages and injunctions; criminal penalties in serious cases.

whatYouMustDo: Check whether your AI training data is covered by the text-and-data-mining rules.
Respect machine-readable opt-outs from rights holders.
Be careful about ownership and infringement when you generate AI content commercially.
keyDates: Text-and-data-mining rules in force since 7 June 2021.
urhg.penalties: Civil claims for damages and injunctions; criminal penalties for serious infringement.

whatYouMustDo: Make sure AI-generated advertising is not misleading.
Label automated commercial content where needed.
Avoid using AI in ways that unfairly harm competitors or consumers.
keyDates: In force; frequently updated.
uwg.penalties: Injunctions, removal of profits, and damages; fines for certain consumer breaches.

whatYouMustDo: If you have market power, do not use AI to put your own services ahead of others unfairly.
Do not misuse data to block competitors.
Watch for dominance built on data and network effects.
keyDates: The Section 19a powers have been in force since 19 January 2021.
gwb.penalties: Up to 10% of worldwide annual turnover.

whatYouMustDo: Make clear, fair contracts for AI services and set out who is liable if the AI fails.
Do not use AI to create deepfakes that harm someone's personality rights.
Tell consumers when prices or terms are set by AI.
keyDates: In force since 1900; continuously updated.
bgb.penalties: Civil liability: damages, injunctions, and contract remedies.

whatYouMustDo: Test AI used in hiring or customer decisions for discrimination.
Make sure AI does not disadvantage people based on protected traits.
Keep records that show your AI decisions are fair.
keyDates: In force since 18 August 2006.
agg.penalties: Compensation and damages claims; the burden of proof can shift to you.

whatYouMustDo: Involve the works council before you introduce AI tools that can monitor or affect staff.
Get a co-determination agreement for performance-monitoring or hiring AI.
Give the works council the information it needs, and expert support if required.
keyDates: AI provisions clarified by the 2021 Works Council Modernisation Act.
betrvg.penalties: Measures introduced without agreement can be blocked or reversed by the labour courts.

whatYouMustDo: Include AI in your workplace risk assessment, including stress from monitoring and algorithmic management.
Reduce the risks you find and review them regularly.
keyDates: In force since 1996; last updated in 2024.
arbschg.penalties: Fines and, in serious cases, criminal liability for employers.

whatYouMustDo: Do not create or deploy AI that produces illegal content such as harmful deepfakes, defamation, or incitement.
Have safeguards to prevent your AI being used for fraud or harassment.
keyDates: In force; a dedicated deepfake offence is being prepared in 2026.
stgb.penalties: Criminal: fines or imprisonment depending on the offence.

whatYouMustDo: Disclose when an account or content is automated, for example a bot that looks like a real person.
Keep recommendation systems on media platforms transparent and non-discriminatory.
keyDates: In force since 7 November 2020.
mstv.penalties: Measures and fines from the state media authorities.

whatYouMustDo: Manage the risks of AI used in credit scoring, trading and other decisions under your risk framework.
Keep clear responsibility and documentation for algorithmic decisions.
Follow BaFin's expectations for outsourcing and risk management.
keyDates: In force; BaFin Big Data and AI principles from 2021.

whatYouMustDo: Govern AI used in underwriting and claims under your risk-management system.
Document and validate the models you use.
Keep human oversight of automated insurance decisions.
keyDates: In force (VAG 2016).

whatYouMustDo: Get BfArM approval for an AI-based medical app you want reimbursed.
Show evidence of a positive healthcare effect.
Meet data-protection, security and medical-device requirements.
keyDates: DiGA fast-track available since 2020.
sgbv_diga.penalties: Removal from the DiGA directory and loss of reimbursement; medical-device penalties.

whatYouMustDo: Decide whether your AI counts as a medical device.
Complete the conformity assessment and obtain CE marking.
Run post-market surveillance and report incidents.
keyDates: Applies since 26 May 2021, with transition periods.
mdr.penalties: National fines, market withdrawal, and loss of CE marking.

whatYouMustDo: Get approval from the KBA for Level 3 and Level 4 automated driving functions.
Meet the operating and technical-supervisor rules in the ordinance.
Keep safety documentation for the driving system.
keyDates: Level 3 framework 2017; Level 4 amendment 28 July 2021; ordinance in force 1 July 2022.
stvg_autonomous.penalties: Approval refusal or withdrawal, fines, and liability for accidents.

whatYouMustDo: Only use fully automated decisions where a law allows it.
Make sure automated decisions can be explained and challenged.
Give reasons and a right to be heard.
keyDates: The automated-decision rule (Section 35a) has been in force since 2017.
vwvfg.penalties: Decisions can be overturned by administrative courts; consequences in public procurement.

whatYouMustDo: Treat AI-integrated products as potentially defective and keep safety evidence.
From 9 December 2026, treat software and AI themselves as products: keep testing and safety evidence, and be ready to disclose technical information if someone brings a claim.
Review your insurance and contracts: the new law no longer caps liability.
keyDates: Current version in force since 1 January 1990.
New version passed by the Bundestag on 8 October 2026 and cleared by the Bundesrat on 16 October 2026; it applies from 9 December 2026.
Products placed on the market up to 8 December 2026 stay under the old rules.
prodhaftg.penalties: Strict liability: compensation for damage caused by a defective product. From 9 December 2026 there is no upper limit (previously EUR 85 million for personal injury) and no EUR 500 deductible for property damage.

whatYouMustDo: If you build health AI, access health data only through the proper national bodies and permits.
Follow the rules for secondary use of health data for research and training.
Keep this alongside your GDPR duties.
keyDates: In force 2025; phased application.
ehds.penalties: National fines and loss of data access.

whatYouMustDo: If you have 50 or more staff, run a confidential internal reporting channel.
Protect people who report legal violations, including unsafe or unlawful AI use, from retaliation.
Route AI-governance concerns through these channels.
keyDates: In force; channels required for organisations with 50 or more staff.
hinschg.penalties: Fines up to 50,000 euros for missing channels or for retaliation.

whatYouMustDo: Keep clear human responsibility for AI-driven financial decisions.
Use good quality data and check models for bias.
Validate models before use and re-validate them regularly.
Monitor performance and keep meaningful human oversight.
keyDates: Based on BaFin guidance from 2021; expectations continue to evolve.

whatYouMustDo: Follow the bill through parliament and prepare policies against harmful deepfakes.
keyDates: Federal cabinet approved the bill on 7 October 2026; it now goes to the Bundestag and Bundesrat. Not yet in force.
deepfake_law.penalties: Not yet set; expected to be criminal penalties.
